attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing Yang-Mills estimate is the reflection-plane trace modulus for the locked gauge-invariant algebra. Existing multiscale bounds plausibly control separated bulk correlations, but they do not automatically control the limit where reflected supports collide, Wilson loops acquire cusps at the plane, or composite curvature observables require boundary-sensitive renormalization.
steps: Fix a finite family \(F_1,\dots,F_n\in\mathcal A_+\) and coefficients \(c\in\mathbb C^n\). The target OS inequality is \(Q_S(F,c)\ge0\).

For \(\delta>0\), replace each observable by its collar translate \(F_i^\delta=T_\delta F_i\in\mathcal A_+^\delta\). This avoids the reflection plane and makes the regulated reflection-positive inequality directly applicable for all sufficiently fine cutoffs.
At cutoff level, reflection positivity gives \(Q_{a,L}^{\delta}(F,c)\ge0\). This is valid before the continuum limit and uses only the regulated positive-time algebra.
Use the domination hypothesis \(\tau_{RG}\succeq\tau_{OS}(\mathcal A_+^\delta)\) to pass to the limit at fixed \(\delta\): \(Q_S(T_\delta F,c)=\lim Q_{a,L}^{\delta}(F,c)\ge0\).
If the trace modulus \(|Q_S(T_\delta F,c)-Q_S(F,c)|\le\omega_F(\delta)\|c\|^2\) is available, let \(\delta\downarrow0\) and obtain \(Q_S(F,c)\ge0\).

Because the argument applies to every finite family and coefficient vector, it would give OS positivity for the continuum gauge-invariant Schwinger functions and hence the OS reconstruction pre-Hilbert space.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation is valid as a conditional theorem, but it has not proved that Balaban/RG cutoff-removal estimates dominate the OS trace seminorms uniformly as \(\delta\downarrow0\). It also has not excluded a same-theory failure in which the collar limit exists only after adding boundary counterterms that were not present in the original gauge-invariant observable.

assumptions: For every cutoff \((a,L)\), the regulated Wilson/Yang-Mills measure or transfer-matrix construction is reflection positive for all embedded collar observables \(\iota_{a,L}(F_i)\).

For each fixed \(\delta>0\) and finite collar family \(F_1,\dots,F_n\in\mathcal A_+^\delta\), the RG cutoff-removal topology implies convergence of the reflected quadratic form \(Q_{a,L}^\delta(F,c)\to Q_S^\delta(F,c)\).

The continuum functional has a trace/collar modulus: for each finite family \(F_i\in\mathcal A_+\), \(Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\to Q_S(F,c)\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\), uniformly for \(c\) in bounded subsets of \(\mathbb C^n\).
Gauge-invariant composite renormalization does not introduce uncancelled reflection-plane counterterms that are invisible to the collar algebra.
definitions: source object: a net \(S_{a,L}\) of regulated gauge-invariant Schwinger functionals on one fixed abstract observable algebra \(\mathcal A\), with positive-time collar subalgebras \(\mathcal A_+^\delta\subset \mathcal A_+\) and reflection \(\Theta\).

target object: a continuum Schwinger functional \(S\) on the same gauge-invariant Euclidean test algebra such that \(Q_S(F,c)\ge 0\) for all finite \(F_i\in\mathcal A_+\), giving the OS pre-Hilbert space before any Hamiltonian or mass-gap argument is invoked.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions through two maps: cutoff removal on fixed collars \(\delta>0\), followed by the valid \(\delta\downarrow0\) trace passage at the reflection plane.

same-theory condition: the embeddings \(\iota_{a,L}:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A_{a,L}\) and collar translations \(T_\delta:\mathcal A_+\to\mathcal A_+^\delta\) commute with gauge-invariant renormalization, reflection, and the continuum identification, so the limiting observable is not replaced by a gauge-fixed, quotient, or boundary-renormalized different theory.

For \(\delta>0\), \(\mathcal A_+^\delta\) denotes gauge-invariant observables whose smearing support lies in \(\{x_0\ge \delta\}\); \(T_\delta F\) is the positive time translation/collar regularization of \(F\).
The OS quadratic form is \(Q_S(F,c)=\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j S((\Theta F_i)^*F_j)\), with the product interpreted in the Euclidean gauge-invariant test algebra.

equations.label: regulated collar positivity
equations.valid_when: Valid for \(F_i\in\mathcal A_+^\delta\), \(a\ll\delta\), finite volume large enough to contain supports, and a reflection-positive lattice or regulated construction.

equations.label: fixed-collar dominated cutoff passage
equations.valid_when: Valid exactly when the actual RG convergence topology dominates the finite OS seminorm determined by the reflected collar probe \((F,c,\delta)\).

equations.label: closed cone on each collar
equations.valid_when: Valid after the previous two hypotheses; this is the formal closed-cone step and contains no further Yang-Mills dynamics.

equations.label: reflection-plane trace modulus
equations.valid_when: Valid only if Schwinger distributions have controlled boundary values as reflected supports approach the plane and contact/cusp counterterms are either absent, already included in the same observable, or positive-compatible.

equations.label: full OS positivity
equations.valid_when: Valid when collar positivity holds for every \(\delta>0\) and the trace modulus holds for the chosen full positive-time finite family.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any gauge-invariant finite family \(F_i\in\mathcal A_+\) for which all shifted collar forms are nonnegative but \(Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\) has no valid limit equal to \(Q_S(F,c)\), or whose limit differs because boundary renormalization changes the observable.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma separates the already-formal closed-cone preservation from the nontrivial Yang-Mills estimate at the reflection plane. It is the bridge from regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms to OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions without changing the observable theory.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Collar-to-plane OS extension lemma: Suppose a cutoff Yang-Mills net of gauge-invariant Schwinger functionals is reflection positive on every positive-time collar algebra, converges to a continuum functional in a topology dominating all fixed-collar reflected quadratic forms, and the continuum functional has a reflection-plane trace modulus for collar translations. Then the continuum Schwinger functional is OS reflection positive on the full positive-time gauge-invariant test algebra.

assumptions: The observable embeddings are fixed before taking limits.
The regulated functionals are reflection positive on \(\mathcal B_+\).
The continuum candidate \(S\) is the \(\tau_{RG}\)-limit of a subnet of \(S_{a,L}\).
definitions: \(\tau_{OS}(\mathcal B_+)\) is the initial topology generated by seminorms \(S\mapsto |Q_S(F,c)|\) for finite \(F_i\in\mathcal B_+\).
\(\tau_{RG}\) is the topology supplied by multiscale compactness and cutoff removal.
Domination means \(S_{a,L}\to S\) in \(\tau_{RG}\) implies \(S_{a,L}\to S\) in \(\tau_{OS}(\mathcal B_+)\).

equations.label: topology domination
equations.valid_when: Valid for the chosen subalgebra only; it can fail for larger algebras with nonlocal Wilson loops or boundary-touching composite fields.

equations.label: cone closure
equations.latex: \mathcal C_{OS}(\mathcal B_+)=\{S:Q_S(F,c)�\ge0\ \forall(F,c)\}\text{ is closed in }\tau_{OS}(\mathcal B_+)
equations.valid_when: Valid because \(\mathcal C_{OS}\) is an intersection of closed half-spaces defined by finite quadratic forms.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If \(\tau_{RG}\) controls ordinary Euclidean correlations but not the reflected product \((\Theta F)^*G\), the closed cone result is irrelevant to OS positivity.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This criterion tells which analytic estimates must be extracted from Balaban-style bounds: not all distributional convergence is enough, only convergence seen by reflected OS quadratic probes.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Reflected-probe domination criterion: OS positivity survives cutoff removal on a subalgebra \(\mathcal B_+\subseteq\mathcal A_+\) if and only if every finite reflected quadratic probe on \(\mathcal B_+\) is continuous for the actual cutoff-removal topology after the fixed observable identification.

assumptions: The continuum observable algebra includes the renormalized limits of the regulated gauge-invariant observables.
Boundary counterterms, if present, are part of the same abstract observable and are not inserted after the positivity proof.
Odd reflection-plane terms cannot appear with arbitrary finite subtraction constants.
definitions: Let \(R_a\) be the cutoff-to-continuum renormalization map on gauge-invariant composite observables.
Let \(B\) denote possible reflection-plane supported counterterms arising as collar supports collide.
Reflection compatibility means \(\Theta R_aF=R_a\Theta F+o(1)\) in every OS probe seminorm.

equations.label: renormalization commutator requirement
equations.valid_when: Valid if renormalization is local, gauge invariant, and reflection covariant in the OS topology, not merely in ordinary distribution topology.

equations.label: allowed boundary correction
equations.valid_when: Valid only for boundary/contact terms whose matrix is positive semidefinite; an indefinite \(M\) is an immediate falsifier for the bridge.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a necessary gauge-invariant boundary subtraction with an indefinite matrix in the OS quadratic form.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma converts the vague same-theory condition into a checkable algebraic condition on renormalized gauge-invariant observables near the reflection plane.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Reflection-compatible renormalization lemma: Composite renormalization preserves the same-theory OS bridge only if the renormalization map is block-diagonal with respect to the reflection-even/odd boundary decomposition, or any boundary mixing has a positive semidefinite contribution to the OS quadratic form.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if a natural gauge-invariant observable, especially a Wilson loop or curvature composite touching the reflection plane, requires an indefinite boundary counterterm or lacks a regulator-independent collar limit.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves a uniform estimate \(|Q_S(T_\delta F,c)-Q_S(F,c)|\le\omega_F(\delta)\|c\|^2\) for a dense gauge-invariant positive-time algebra and verifies RG domination of all fixed-collar reflected probes.
control_decision.reason: Do not pivot yet: the branch now has a precise falsifiable analytic obligation, namely the collar trace modulus. The closed-cone machinery is valid but exhausted; future work should target the boundary/contact estimate rather than restating topology closure.

dependency_updates.description: Split into a formal fixed-collar closed-cone passage and a non-formal \(\delta\downarrow0\) trace/collar estimate. The bridge is valid only when both parts hold.

The algebra must be locked before cutoff removal and must contain collar translates of each full positive-time observable. Boundary-renormalized replacements are not allowed unless included in the original same-theory algebra.

Ordinary distributional convergence is insufficient; the topology must dominate finite reflected quadratic probes on every collar and provide uniform control needed for the reflection-plane trace limit.
New explicit dependency: control of contact, cusp, and composite-renormalization terms when reflected supports collide at the OS plane.

falsifiers: falsifier: construct a sequence of gauge-invariant Wilson-loop collar observables \(T_\delta W\) for which \(Q_S(T_\delta W,c)\ge0\) for every \(\delta>0\) but the limit as \(\delta\downarrow0\) is divergent, regulator-dependent, or not equal to the intended \(Q_S(W,c)\).

falsifier: show that the RG compactness topology controls separated Schwinger distributions but not the product distribution \((\Theta T_\delta F)^*T_\delta G\) uniformly as supports approach the reflection plane.
falsifier: find an unavoidable gauge-invariant reflection-plane counterterm with an indefinite matrix contribution to the OS quadratic form.

falsifier: prove lattice reflection positivity only for transfer-matrix cylinder functions while the continuum test algebra uses smeared curvature composites or Wilson loops not approximable in the same positive-time algebra.

falsifier: demonstrate that the collar translation \(T_\delta\) fails to commute with the continuum observable identification, so the limiting positive forms concern a different observable than the one appearing in the Yang-Mills Schwinger functions.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 172 identifies the first genuinely non-tautological bridge after the closed-cone observation. Fixed-collar OS positivity is formally preserved once RG convergence is valid for reflected probes; the hard part is extending from collars to the reflection plane without changing the theory. The decisive estimate is a trace modulus for \(Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\to Q_S(F,c)\). This reframes the branch: reflection positivity is not merely closedness of a cone, but closedness plus a boundary-value theorem for gauge-invariant observables as reflected supports collide.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Work on a model finite family: two smeared curvature-square observables supported near \(x_0=0\). Translate them to collars, express the reflected quadratic form as a separated four-point distribution, and test whether known multiscale bounds imply a \(\delta\downarrow0\) modulus or whether a reflection-plane contact counterterm appears.

Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
